We prioritize an environment where people can feel comfortable and accepted without the pressure to use intoxicants, and everyone is invited. Led by Zanny, our Mindful Recovery Support Groups gather twice daily, at 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM, with sessions built around guided meditation, a reading, open sharing, and community connection, and peers available at night to be present with you. Every booth tells a story. Every piece is shaped by the hands and imagination of its creator. Leave a little room in your schedule for discovery.

f: From breakfast biscuits before your first set to seafood, barbecue, vegan Japanese comfort food, handcrafted açaí bowls, and late-night festival snacks, the 2026 food program brings together returning favorites, beloved local businesses, and a handful of exciting newcomers making their farm debut.

Many of these vendors have become part of the fabric of Pickathon itself. Ate-Oh-Ate has been feeding festivalgoers for more than a decade. Obon returns with its acclaimed vegan Japanese cuisine. Bombay Station brings its eclectic blend of Thai-inspired flavors all the way from Colorado. Fitts Seafoods returns with sustainably sourced Pacific Northwest seafood, while Pine State, Sweet Leaf, Smoke & Brine, Herbal Junction, and PS & Qs continue their long-running Pickathon traditions.

This year also welcomes several new additions to the farm. Festivalgoers can discover the playful hot dog creations of Cobra Dogs, fresh coastal seafood from Flying Fish, house-made sandwiches from Sandy O’s, nostalgic frozen lemonade from Junior Lemon, and warm mini donuts from Donut Drop.
Whether you’re looking for a quick bite between stages or planning your entire festival weekend around meals (we know you’re out there), you’ll find something worth seeking out.
Here’s a first taste of who’s coming to the farm this year:
Market Row Ate-Oh-Ate Bombay Station Carioca Bowls Cobra Dogs Fitts Seafoods Obon Pine State Ps & Qs Sandy O’s Smoke & Brine Sweet Leaf
Lucky Barn Let’s Roll Poblano Wrapped
Come hungry, and bring your curiosity. You know: the food at Pickathon is its own kind of headliner.
For those looking for an even deeper culinary experience, Curation returns in 2026.

Hidden among the trees, Curation pairs acclaimed chefs with intimate live performances from Pickathon artists for a one-of-a-kind dining experience. Part dinner party, part concert, and entirely unique to Pickathon, these gatherings offer a rare chance to slow down, connect, and experience the festival from a different perspective.
With just 100 seats available for each event, Curation remains one of the most sought-after experiences on the farm.

stories.t: The New Farmhouse Stage: A Love Letter to Portland
stories.x: The Farmhouse has always been the front door to Pendarvis Farm. This year, it’s got a stage. New for 2026, the Farmhouse Stage is an all-Portland lineup.
stories.b: The Farmhouse is the literal front door to Pendarvis Farm — the first thing you pass through when you arrive, the threshold where the outside world starts to fall away. This year, that threshold gets a stage. Designed by Bora Architecture & Interiors as part of their collaboration with Dream Big Cit
f: The Farmhouse is the literal front door to Pendarvis Farm — the first thing you pass through when you arrive, the threshold where the outside world starts to fall away. This year, that threshold gets a stage.

Designed by Bora Architecture & Interiors as part of their collaboration with Dream Big City, the new Farmhouse Stage is nestled into the arrival experience, intimate, welcoming, and built for the kind of music that pulls you in before you even realize you’ve stopped walking. And all weekend long, it belongs entirely to Portland.
The Farmhouse Stage is our love letter to Portland.

All weekend long, the stage at the festival’s front door belongs to the artists who call the Pacific Northwest home — a curated lineup spanning folk, roots, indie pop, soul, psych-rock, and everything in between.

Thursday kicks off with the Portland Songwriters Guild, a collective of original voices representing the best of what’s coming out of the Portland scene right now. Expect the full range: Ronnie Carrier’s powerful folk-rock storytelling (her song “Idle Hands” just won the 2026 Local Roots Songwriting Contest), Nico Avery’s intimate heartbreak songs, Kyle Glenn’s alt-country narratives, Aika Collins’ doo-wop-twisted bummers, Vandana Prabhakar’s math-rock-inflected acoustic pop, Nathan Earle’s rye-soaked rambler wisdom, Lisa Fitzgerald’s sweet and deeply personal melodies, Friendmaker’s spare and introspective journal songs, Shiloh Mae’s lyric-forward indie folk, Leo Moon’s haunting urban prairie tunes (and founding member of Blitzen Trapper), Linoy Yichieli’s alt-pop soul, and Zach Markezich’s heartfelt genre-hopping songwriting.

Friday brings the full-band energy: Vista House delivering open-range alt-country, Presidio with their raw psych-rock and cinematic indie pop, Taylor Kingman and The Electric Skeleton (of TK & The Holy Know-Nothings) with unflinching songwriting that howls and whispers in equal measure, Rose Gerber blending country and alt-rock in a sound where cowboy boots meet Doc Martens, Kendall Lujan drawing from jazz, folk, bossa nova, and indie-rock on her newly released debut album, and Mama Sam & The Jam bringing their dreamy, groove-forward psychedelic folk-pop ahead of their debut LP drop this fall.

Saturday closes things out with Ozkat-Ozkat’s improvisational jazz quartet, Lynna Corinne’s sea island-rooted country, Reb & the Good News and their soul-funk grooves and horn lines built for dancing, Mark Tegio’s barroom poetry in the tradition of Townes Van Zandt and Tom Waits, AC Sapphire’s cosmic Americana and whole-hearted songwriting, and Ringer & the Bells closing it all out with rhythmic, melodic exploration.
Your people are playing the farm.

These are the artists your Portland friends already know and love, now playing just down the road at Pendarvis Farm. The Farmhouse Stage was designed for community, the kind that shows up early, stays late, and discovers something new on the way in.
If you’ve ever thought about coming to Pickathon, this is your sign. Bring your people. This stage was made for you.

stories.t: Pickathon 2026 Neighborhood Reveal: The Farmhouse & Orchard
stories.x: The structures arriving at Pendarvis Farm this July are on a longer journey. Designed by Bora Architecture & Interiors in partnership with Dream Big City, they’ll move from the festival grounds to Dream Plaza 2.0, a community skate and arts space taking shape
stories.b: Rooted in Place Two sites, two organizations committed to bringing community together through hands-on placemaking and event-based activation. Portland Dream Plaza and Pickathon share a connection to agriculture through their locations: the former in the Produce Row in Portland's Central Eastside an
f: Two sites, two organizations committed to bringing community together through hands-on placemaking and event-based activation. Portland Dream Plaza and Pickathon share a connection to agriculture through their locations: the former in the Produce Row in Portland’s Central Eastside and the latter at Pendarvis Farm in Happy Valley.

Working with Dream Big City and Creative Neighborhoods, the design team was inspired by the parallels between their ethos and the grocer trade: growth, modularity, and network. This led to a design made up of simple components transportable to different sites, fit for aggregation into larger structures, and ready to be animated by activities.

From seating modules to segments of a half-pipe, different components designed for Portland Dream Plaza version 2.0 will go on a journey from prefabrication to temporary use at the festival to their final destination at SE 9th and Taylor. At each stop, the reconfiguration of the parts and pieces and the potential for participatory artmaking will result in a custom design specific to that site as well as the opportunity to tell the stories of skate culture, creative reuse, and partnership.

At the Farmhouse and Orchard Neighborhoods of Pickathon, these components will take the form of story poles, a busking stage, a ticket booth, and a series of archways, transporting folks into the spheres of the festival.

After the festival, they’ll eventually make up Dream Plaza 2.0, which will be a safe, community-centered space that brings people of all ages together through not just skateboarding, but also artmaking and performing. Community engagement sessions and dialogue with skateboarders, youth and families are shaping this plaza into Portland’s most welcoming third space that embraces community and enriches Portland’s vibrant culture. Keep an eye out for updates!

The path between Dream Plaza and Pickathon that the components traverse will physically imprint on them along with colors representing discovery, energy, and belonging – values everyone involved in this process hopes to embody.

Among the structures making their way to Pendarvis Farm this year is a brand new busking stage, situated right in the heart of the Farmhouse neighborhood. New for 2026, it will be programmed entirely with Portland artists all weekend long — from the Portland Songwriters Guild on Thursday to full bands like Rose Gerber, Mama Sam & The Jam, Vista House, AC Sapphire, and more across Friday and Saturday. A fitting first impression at the festival’s front door.
Click here to learn more about the Farmhouse live performances this year!

Bora Architecture & Interiors is an award-winning national design practice based in Portland, Oregon. With health, equity and sustainability essential to their pursuit of inspiring architecture, they are committed to creating transformative environments that shape communities and elevate the human experience.

They pride themselves on thoughtfully crafted design that sparks curiosity and brings people together. Their love for the arts influences their work, infusing design in such a way that each project tells a unique and creative story. They also recognize design as a platform and responsibility, one in which they can play an active role in making our world more just and equitable.

The value they place on nature, sustainability and authenticity stems from their roots in the Pacific Northwest. Their surroundings have both grounded and inspired them while propelling a design reputation that has opened doors to work throughout the country. Through their diverse work they embrace every opportunity to advocate for meaningful spaces in which all communities can thrive.

stories.t: The Travelin’ McCourys Are Coming to Pickathon 2026
stories.x: The Travelin’ McCourys are joining the 2026 Pickathon lineup for a late-night Sunday set worth staying up for.
stories.b: Some announcements just land differently. This is one of them. The Travelin' McCourys are joining the 2026 Pickathon lineup, closing out the Cherry Hill Stage on Sunday night at 11pm. Ronnie and Rob McCoury, Alan Bartram, Cody Kilby, and Christian Ward, one of the most respected bands in bluegrass,
f: Some announcements just land differently. This is one of them.

The Travelin’ McCourys are joining the 2026 Pickathon lineup, closing out the Cherry Hill Stage on Sunday night at 11pm. Ronnie and Rob McCoury, Alan Bartram, Cody Kilby, and Christian Ward, one of the most respected bands in bluegrass, bringing everything they have to Pendarvis Farm.
Rooted in Tradition, Fluent in What Happens Next

The Travelin’ McCourys carry the weight of serious bluegrass lineage, Ronnie and Rob are sons of Del McCoury, one of the genre’s true living legends, and they wear it without being trapped by it. This is a band that knows where it comes from and isn’t afraid of where a set might go. Tight harmonies built over decades of playing together. Solos that take chances. Setlists that breathe and shift and find their own shape over the course of a night.

The Cherry Hill Stage on a Sunday at 11pm is exactly the right setting. Late, open air, the weekend winding toward something final and memorable. The Travelin’ McCourys have a gift for that kind of moment.
We’ll say this much: there’s more to the story. Something special is in the works for the weekend beyond the Sunday closing set, and we’re not ready to share it yet. Keep your eyes on this space.

The Travelin’ McCourys are the kind of act that fills in a lineup and also lifts it. If you’ve been waiting for a reason to commit to Pickathon 2026, July 30 through August 2 at Pendarvis Farm in Happy Valley, Oregon, consider this it.
Tickets are on sale now at pickathon.com, including the Buy Now, Pay Later option if you want to lock in your spot and spread out the cost.
This one is going to be something people talk about. 🐸

stories.t: Pickathon Is for the Kids: Captain Coyote’s Frog Bog
stories.x: Meet the performers, hands-on activities, and imaginative worlds waiting for your little adventurers at this year’s Coyote Neighborhood.
stories.b: A Festival Within a Festival We have so much family programming that we've created an entire kids festival inside a festival. Our family-focused Coyote Neighborhood, tucked into the woods above Cherry Hill, has become one of Pickathon's most beloved spaces the past four years. This year, it's gettin
f: We have so much family programming that we’ve created an entire kids festival inside a festival. Our family-focused Coyote Neighborhood, tucked into the woods above Cherry Hill, has become one of Pickathon’s most beloved spaces the past four years. This year, it’s getting a whole new world.
Welcome to Captain Coyote’s Frog Bog.

The Coyote Neighborhood is transforming into a bustling bog where Pickathon’s youngest adventurers can play, create and explore. Our fearless leader, Captain Coyote, has discovered a pristine bog full of frogs, cattails, lily pads, nurse logs, spider webs, and more. With stage sets, play structures and art installations built by Cedarwood Waldorf School and our resident artists, kids will step into a world of imaginative play as they explore the bog.

In celebration of Pickathon’s 2026 frog mascot, kids will make frog crafts and noisemakers with Crafty Critters! They’ll also work on collaborative projects with Making Earth Cool, an arts collective inspiring people to be better stewards of planet Earth, in preparation for our Sunday afternoon Puppet Parade.
Family Music on the Coyote Stage
The Coyote Stage will host interactive performances by renowned family artists all day long on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

This year’s lineup includes two recent GRAMMY-winners: Fyütch, with his joyful, social-justice-infused hip hop and R&B, and 123 Andrés, sharing energetic, bilingual songs and sounds from all corners of Latin America. We also have GRAMMY-nominees Aaron Nigel Smith, who blends reggae, folk and country, and Flor Bromley, who weaves together Latin American rhythms and global sounds.

Local Portland favorites Red Yarn (roots-rock and puppetry), Mo Phillips & the Spaghetti Pants Dance Band(hilarious kindie jams), and Sing with Teacher Brittany (bilingual, trauma-informed songs for families) round out the Coyote Stage lineup. For the second year in a row, we’ll host a Family Square Dance featuring Steph Noll calling with youth string band, Triple File. In the early evening, the stage shifts to youth programming – click here to view the schedule.
Beloved Portland “kindie” performer Red Yarn curates the entire Coyote experience alongside a dedicated team of artists and educators.

Family music offerings will stretch beyond the Coyote Stage. Music Together of Portland will offer music classes each morning, while My Voice Music will lead workshops and facilitate a talent show on Sunday. We’ll even have a family-friendly stand-up comedy set by Jokey Jokes with David DaCosta!

Each morning begins with Family Yoga. For very young kids and their caregivers, the Bridgetown Baby Family Feeding Nest offers a shady, quiet nook for nursing parents to relax. Cedarwood will offer drop-off childcare sessions at their little school in the woods. Returning favorites Trackers Earth will take kids on wilderness adventures for an hour at a time, teaching foam archery, hands-on folk crafts, and role-playing games. Sellwood Community House will engage youth with a new teen volunteer program. The Traveling Typist will share the magic of typewriters as he composes collaborative stories with kids.
Because we prioritize families at Pickathon, tickets for kids 12 and under are still FREE when attending with family, and teens 13-17 are 1/2 price when attending for the weekend.
Follow us @pickathon and @pickathoncoyote for real-time updates. See you in Captain Coyote’s Frog Bog, young adventurers!

stories.t: Pickathon Film Crew Announcement
stories.x: This one comes from the heart. A note on our film crew, what’s changing in 2026, and what we’re working toward.
stories.b: For almost two decades, Pickathon has approached capturing the magic of the festival in a way that matched the creative spirit of the event itself, telling the story of who we are as a community. A group that lives without gravity for four days in the woods of Pendarvis Farm. Those of you who have e
f: For almost two decades, Pickathon has approached capturing the magic of the festival in a way that matched the creative spirit of the event itself, telling the story of who we are as a community. A group that lives without gravity for four days in the woods of Pendarvis Farm.

Those of you who have experienced our livestreams from afar know the unconventional approach Pickathon’s film crew has shared with the world. This style of storytelling was groundbreaking. It wasn’t traditional live video simply documenting music or festivalgoers, and it wasn’t a promotional piece. It was something entirely its own.

It has been a journey told through lenses, lighting, sound, and an incredible crew that, at its peak, included more than 700 industry professionals from around the world. Together, they created an artistic vision that extended across physical and digital media platforms alike. Check out our YouTube channel to look into our world.

Since the pandemic, the ways people consume these stories, along with the costs required to produce this collaborative art form, have changed dramatically. Unfortunately, those realities have created a financial hardship that Pickathon is unable to support at this time.

While we are actively working with partners to bring this program back in 2027, Pickathon will not have the robust film production in 2026, and sadly, we will not have a large staff or volunteer film crew this year. This will not be the last you hear from the film crew. We will return to share these amazing moments with you again soon.
If you or someone you know is interested in helping bring this program back, we’d love to hear from you. Contact info@pickathon.com.

stories.t: Starburst: A Backstage Neighborhood Under the Stars
stories.x: Starburst is a new pavilion rising above The Bluff at Pickathon 2026 — eleven timber modules, a folded canopy framing Mt. Hood, and a backstage neighborhood built for those inside the circle. Patron Pass holders only.
stories.b: Floating on the bluff above the Galaxy Barn, Starburst, designed as both shelter and spatial marker within the landscape, forms part of a backstage neighborhood at the southern edge of the Pickathon site. The pavilion is composed of eleven flexible timber modules built from plywood and dimensional l
f: Floating on the bluff above the Galaxy Barn, Starburst, designed as both shelter and spatial marker within the landscape, forms part of a backstage neighborhood at the southern edge of the Pickathon site. The pavilion is composed of eleven flexible timber modules built from plywood and dimensional lumber, creating a rhythmic field of shade, gathering, and pause beneath the open sky. The overall folded roof form further organizes these modules into a gentle curve that responds to the existing topography and intentionally frames views toward Mt. Hood, anchoring the experience of the structure within its wider regional landscape.

For those who haven’t explored it before: The Bluff is one of Pickathon’s backstage neighborhoods — a shaded hillside perch among towering Douglas Firs, overlooking the Paddock stage and the forest below. It functions as an intimate hillside lounge, and a peaceful threshold into the main camping grounds. Starburst sits within the backstage neighborhood exclusive to Patron Pass holders.

The design draws from a celestial narrative where shifting light, color, and structure evoke the experience of moving through a constellation of spaces. Each module operates as a fragment of a larger whole, together forming an undulating canopy that transitions from daytime refuge to a luminous nighttime environment. Donated furnishings help transform the space into a comfortable backstage retreat for artists, patrons, and festival staff alike.

Embodying Pickathon’s commitment to community impact, Starburst is conceived for a second life from the outset. After its role at Pickathon, the entire structure will be carefully disassembled and reconfigured downstream at The Showdown, where it will become a permanent shaded patio cover, extending its presence beyond the festival as a lasting piece of community infrastructure.
In this way, Starburst bridges festival and future, temporary and permanent, anchoring itself within Pickathon’s evolving constellation while carrying its story forward into a new setting.

Starburst is part of the backstage neighborhood accessible exclusively to Patron Pass holders. This isn’t standard VIP — it’s an invitation into the inner workings of the festival, shared with the artists and crew who make it happen.

Artist Village Access — Complimentary catering and beverages shared with the artists and crew. The Inside Track — Access to backstage hospitality at every stage and entry to exclusive pop-up performances. Ultimate Ease — Includes Wednesday Early Arrival and a dedicated Express Concierge for check-in. Get your Patron Pass →

stories.t: Were we not alone?
stories.x: In 2026, a collection of massive objects in various states of disrepair were discovered in the woods surrounding Pendarvis Farm. Their purpose and who built them remains a mystery to us.
stories.b: Pickathon has always been full of mysteries, and in 2026 The Grove takes on a new layer of intrigue. f: Pickathon has always been full of mysteries, and in 2026 The Grove takes on a new layer of intrigue. Deep in the woods surrounding Pendarvis Farm, a collection of massive objects—strange and in various states of disrepair—has been discovered. Their purpose, and the identity of whoever built them, remains unknown.

C.H.A.D. and the locals feel the pull—something out there is drawing them in. Designed by WORKS Architecture, The Grove invites you to explore the neighborhood and find C.H.A.D. (Curious Happenings Anomaly Detection) among the relics this weekend, if you dare to look closer.

A massive gateway is largely intact – if slightly akimbo – and can be seen from some distance. It emits an eeire glow which changes in color and brightness throughout a standard solar cycle. It seems to have an unearthly attraction to the uninitiated.

The monumental altar is the most pristine of the discovered objects — untouched by whatever ruin befell the rest. It appears to have been the home of a long-lost ritual. At irregular intervals the locals gather around it to worship the god of unknown power positioned ominously behind it, calling to it with voice and instrument until the woods themselves seem to answer.

Evidence suggests an even larger element once stood here, and was destroyed. Its pieces have since been dragged back and reassembled into a wall that blocks all access to the woods beyond. The work is deliberate. The intent is not.
Who — or what — were they trying to keep out?

Other pieces lie cast far afield from their origin, strewn across the ground as if flung or carried. We know they have been moved. Whether by natural force or unnatural hand, and to what end, we cannot say. The locals return to this place often — both during the sacrifices at the altar, and in the long silences between them.
The fifth object reveals itself only to those who reach the far edge of the site. We are still learning what it is, and what lies on the other side of it.

WORKS Architecture is a Portland and Los Angeles-based firm founded by Principal Carrie Strickland in 2005, built around a collective of design leaders committed to pushing beyond conventional architectural practice. Proudly 100% woman-owned and majority women-staffed, the firm brings a collaborative, multi-perspective approach to a wide range of project types — from pioneering mass-timber construction in Oregon and California to designing the first high-rise in LA’s Arts District. With more than 60 design awards to their name and consistent recognition from AIA, Architizer, and Architect Magazine, WORKS has established itself as one of the Pacific Coast’s most ambitious and award-winning design studios.

stories.t: Mountains of Sound Returns to Pickathon 2026
stories.x: Mountains of Sound returns to Pickathon’s Market neighborhood in 2026 as a 120-frame circular timber pavilion inspired by Wizard Island at the center of Crater Lake. By day a shaded meeting point, after dark a dance floor with sound embedded in every direction
stories.b: Mountains of Sound is back. Now in its second year at Pickathon, the installation anchors the Market neighborhood and the central hub of the festival, where foot traffic converges and people find each other between sets. This year's structure takes its inspiration from Wizard Island, the volcanic ci
f: Now in its second year at Pickathon, the installation anchors the Market neighborhood and the central hub of the festival, where foot traffic converges and people find each other between sets. This year’s structure takes its inspiration from Wizard Island, the volcanic cinder cone at the center of Crater Lake, formed from the same geological forces that shaped the mountains around it.

The mountains that form Oregon’s volcanic history are the state’s navigational backbone, visible from the cities, towns, rivers, forests, and farmlands across the region. Together they are a shared reference point that has drawn people together for generations. They are landmarks in the truest sense: places that tell you where you are and, in doing so, remind you that you’re part of something larger.
Mountains of Sound began with two questions: what if we created our own mountains? And what if we embedded them with interactive, social, and sonic qualities?

Designed by award-winning architecture studio West of West and structural engineers at Holmes, this year’s installation is a tall circular pavilion built from 120 radiating timber frames that sweep low to the ground at the center before rising at the outer edges to create shade.

Up close, the installation is built to be used. Benches run along both the inner and outer edges of the structure, inviting visitors to sit, lean back, and look up through the interlocking timber frames at the sky. By day it functions as a shaded retreat, a place to rest, recharge, and arrange a meeting point amid the energy of the festival. After dark, the character shifts entirely: the dance floor activates, a DJ performs within the crowd, and sound is embedded directly into the structure to fill the space from every direction.

“Mountains of Sound is an installation designed to engage all your senses by creating rhythms of light and shadow throughout the day. And as you move through it, the experience moves with you, nothing is static. Every moment inside it is a different way of experiencing the music.” — Jai Kumaran

The team approached the project’s material use by asking a single question from the start: where will this go next? Past projects have seen festival stages transformed into sleeping pods for veterans and tons of lumber donated to local high schools. Mountains of Sound continues that tradition, conceived from the outset as a future community asset.

West of West is an award-winning architecture practice that engages the worlds of design, art, culture, and technology to shape contemporary life and the built environment at all scales. Founded in Los Angeles, the studio has been named one of the Top 50 Design Firms in North America and recognized as one of the Top 220 Architects in the world. Their research and design process prioritizes listening and clear communication to translate ambitious strategic concepts into impactful architectural solutions, exploring design ideas through project-directed research that integrates craft, materials, form, and proven building practices within a collaborative, stakeholder-driven approach. Their work draws from the unique conditions around each project to create meaningful places.

Holmes pursues bold ideas and possibilities, challenging conventional thinking with creativity, technical expertise, and a hands-on approach to solving tough problems. As structural and fire engineers, Holmes designs with impact, shaping the built world not only through aesthetics and function, but through a deep commitment to sustainability, safety, and resilience. Their work is never done in isolation: Holmes is an active participant in the broader regional, global, and professional conversations that shape our shared built environment. Born in New Zealand more than 65 years ago, Holmes has grown into a distinctively international practice of local partners and global specialists. With more than 500 people worldwide, the firm delivers a powerful combination of innovation, technical excellence, and pragmatic problem-solving.
Mountains of Sound is at Pickathon July 30 – August 2 at Pendarvis Farm in Happy Valley, Oregon. Click here for tickets.

stories.t: Meet the DJs: Pickathon 2026 DJ Lineup, Presented by Daydream
stories.x: Pickathon’s 2026 DJ lineup is here. Meet the 30+ DJs bringing deep crates, global sounds, and late-night dance parties to Pendarvis Farm this July 30 – August 2.
stories.b: Pickathon has always been about discovery. The moment a song you've never heard stops you mid-stride on the path between stages. The afternoon you find yourself dancing in the woods to a record that was pressed in a city you've never visited. The DJ program is where that magic lives most freely, and
f: Pickathon has always been about discovery. The moment a song you’ve never heard stops you mid-stride on the path between stages. The afternoon you find yourself dancing in the woods to a record that was pressed in a city you’ve never visited. The DJ program is where that magic lives most freely, and we are proud to announce the 2026 DJ lineup, presented by Daydream.

This year’s roster spans 30+ artists. Some are Pickathon fixtures whose sets have become part of the festival’s institutional memory. Others are first-timers bringing fresh perspective to Pendarvis Farm. All of them are archivists, historians, and tastemakers. Their crates are deep, their knowledge is hard-won, and their role in the Pickathon experience is irreplaceable. The DJs don’t fill time between acts. They create the connective tissue of the weekend, building context and curiosity that makes discovery possible.
Here’s who’s bringing the music in 2026.

MorningRemorse A selector of vibes from all over the world, Carlos Block-Almazan has been playing records weekly on XRAY.FM since the station’s inception, traveling the globe dropping 7″ jams for bodies to move to. Expect disco, boogie funk, salsa, cumbia, and outsider dance jams.
disco diablo Record devotee and host of Manteca on KMHD, disco diablo spins genre-blurring sets full of thoughtful energy and unexpected gems, guided by a love of filling space with sound.

Oscurita Portland-based Oscurita (Adie Rae) is a genre-blurring intuitive room reader. Raised on a steady diet of jungle and hardcore punk, she is known for her range and eclecticism: left field disco, post-punk, and acid jazz delivered with narrative and patience. Adie also serves as the Pickathon DJ Programming Director and Programming Director at Daydream Wine and Sound.

GREASY A real record junkie since the late 80s, Mat Griesse has been digging for under-appreciated cuts through 60s R&B, Popcorn, Disco, Boogie 12″, Jamaican 45s, Jazz Funk, Garage 45s, and a whole lot of Soul. He founded DUG in 2008, one of Seattle’s best and longest-running dance parties.

Tom Humphrey Hosting the weekly radio show Backroad to Nowhere on XRAY.FM since the station’s inception in 2014, Tom Humphrey explores a musical universe orbiting around folk music, from avant-garde jazz to the vanguard of country. He has been DJing parties and pre-show sets at Pickathon since 2016.

DJ Maaxa & Serene DJ Maaxa is a music anthropologist, radio host, writer, and 25-year veteran behind the decks with roots in the Bay Area funk scene. Her work has been featured in SPIN and the SF Bay Guardian, and she has published books and documentaries on Sufi ritual sound, global hip-hop undergrounds, and women tradition-bearers. Serene, her 13-year-old son and the heir to her record collection, is a musician studying turntablism, percussion, and dance since he was a toddler. This is their third year DJing Pickathon together: rare groove, Afro-funk, rocksteady, spiritual jazz, global house, and underground hip-hop, tag-team style.

Wayward Girls Soul Club An all-female DJ collective serving their favorite records to venues in Portland and beyond since 2019. They play music from the female gaze: R&B, Soul, Funk, Boogaloo, Garage, and much more. You can hear them live every Saturday on XRAY.FM 2–3PM on their long-running show, The In Crowd.

DJ Dentside A country music DJ known for bringing honky-tonk energy to the dance floor, regularly hosting lively nights at the Kenton Club. With a deep love for the genre and its roots, she not only spins crowd-favorite tracks but also books and promotes talented local bands, keeping the spirit of country community alive.

Impact! Sound A DJ crew based in Portland specializing in reggae, ska, and rocksteady. Their sets are delivered on a custom 20,000-watt sound system channeling authentic Jamaican soundsystem culture. Drawing influence from Studio One, Trojan Records, and classic dub traditions, Impact! Sound hosts their weekly show every Saturday on X-Ray FM.

The Ambassador Allen “The Ambassador” Thayer is a music journalist, radio, and club DJ specializing in soul and funk-infused music scenes from around the world, with a deep focus on Brazilian music. He has written about legendary and underground artists for outlets including Wax Poetics, Aquarium Drunkard, and The Fader, and across over a dozen record labels. In Portland, he hosts the weekly Brazilian Beat on KMHD Jazz Radio 89.1 FM, and has held past residencies in NYC and SF with regular opening sets for Jazz Is Dead in LA.

The Country Co-Op The Country Co-Op is a country music DJ collective formed in 2017 and based in Portland. Inspired by dusty outlaw songs and boot-scootin staples, the Co-Op wrangles turntables to introduce people to country music for the first time and reintroduce longtime fans to timeless classics. They play every Sunday at the Sandy Hut and every weekend at the Six Shooter, holding down the dance floor and holding up a deep love for all that is country music.

DJ Honest John A Portland-based party curator with roots in Miami who brings the heat wherever his needle drops. His sets weave together funky disco, bouncy boogie, and smooth grooves. A devotee of deep cuts with an ear for the unexpected, John has hosted Savage Beat on XRAY FM since 2015 and holds down regular spots at Gold Dust Meridian, LaVerne’s, and Daydream.

DJ Lofi A Portland DJ, guitarist in the band Lowfires, and record collector with roots in Detroit. His taste leans toward the fringes: outsider folk, basement punk, private press oddities, and records that feel a little haunted. He hosts The Search for Skip James on Shady Pines Radio, spinning sets that pull threads between past and present.

DJ Maxx Bass Jared White, owner of Clinton Street Records, has spent over 30 years behind the booth. From the legendary Booty Bassment to the Oaks Park skating rink and disco nights at the Sandy Hut, his experience spans iconic dance floors and intimate gatherings alike.

LAFLOR For DJ and radio host LAFLOR (Sabrina Cerquera), the artistry of DJing goes back to its most integral foundation: the roots. She has curated an extensive library of salsa and cumbia paying tribute to her Miamian-Colombian ancestry. Her radio shows have aired through Freeform (PDX), Jolt Radio (MIA), and NTS Radio for Hora De La Flor. She has played gigs in Portland, Colombia, Cuba, and across the U.S., with residencies at Hey Love and Holy Ghost Bar.

Phreaker Fighter Hailing from the Oklahoma prairie and now based in Corvallis, Phreaker Fighter takes great inspiration from the record-slinging legends of Chicago and Detroit. She has rocked PDX mainstay joints including Hickey Machine, Twirl, and Your Sunday Best. An obsessive crate digger, her sets are filled with soulful, raw, funky, jazzy, and obscure gems spanning six decades of underground dance music history.

Jesse Sugar Moore A lifelong record collector, DJ, and half the creative force behind Broken Dreams in Portland’s Alberta Arts District. Jesse has opened for notable acts including Bonobo, Washed Out, Ladymonix, Waajeed, and Mall Grab, and has played every context imaginable: from dive bars to warehouse raves, from weddings to Burning Man.

1-800-WHITTAKER 1-800-WHITTAKER is a local DJ & the owner of the NE Portland record store Music History. Donned a “music archeologist” by KMHD DJs, Whittaker has been traveling the world since his early 20s in search of unearthed musical gems, new & old, from Istanbul to Tokyo. Geoff brings these international sensibilities to his DJ sets, fusing them with dancefloor classics & lesser known gems, spanning every genre under the sun from salsa to R&B. For Pickathon, he will be bringing a mix of R&B, funk, disco, house, & latin sounds.

Nathan Detroit Resident of the legendary Spend The Night party series since 2015, Nathan Detroit has been shaking down dance floors for 20+ years. Traversing the electronic multiverse, with polyrhythmic bass rollers, percussive and broken techno, crispy electro, UK garage, and dub-wise, he curates a vibe uniquely his own.

K Marie A Portland-based curator of vibes known for her seamless, open-format sets that move effortlessly across genres. With over a decade behind the decks, her notable credits include performing on American Idol alongside Janelle Monáe, touring with the Jonas Brothers, and showcasing at Lightning in a Bottle.

Dan Yaker Originally from Albuquerque and now Portland-based, Dan Yaker has been collecting records and playing them since 2007. His style reflects a lifelong love of hip-hop and electronic music, tracing their roots through vintage funk, soul, disco, and jazz. Whether setting a laidback atmosphere at Daydream or bringing the party vibe poolside at Soho House, he’s in his element wherever he’s got a turntable.

DJ Stray A Portland-based DJ with numerous city residencies and national recognition. In 2019, Stray appeared on Sway in the Morning on Sirius XM, with his mix featured as “mix of the week.” With deep crates spanning all genres, he has appeared at the Night Market and James Beard Festival, and plays nightclubs and parties including Motown on Mondays.

Spinitch A Portland born-and-raised producer, MC, and DJ. His latest album “Run for the Arts,” a collaboration with Portland rapper Milc featuring Open Mike Eagle and Blu, streamed hundreds of thousands of times and sold out within a month. An obsessive crate-digger of soul, funk, psych, and hip-hop, he spins sets around town at Keys Lounge, Wax Social, and Daydream.

Flor Violenta A Portland-based DJ spinning cumbia and other Latin sounds for the dancefloor, moving between psychedelic, tropical, and electronic styles while highlighting new interpretations rooted in traditional rhythms. The force behind Cumbia House Party, featured in Portland Mercury’s New Year’s Eve picks, and a former host of Vinyl Pleasures Radio on Freeform Portland.

Mintwhisper A Portland-based DJ with roots in San Diego, influenced by the Bay Area and East Coast. Her selections move through deep house, disco, and soul, shaped by dubby textures and rhythm-forward energy. She hosts The Garden on Samewave Radio, a monthly show exploring warm, groove-forward sounds rooted in nostalgia and shaped by Black and queer dancefloor traditions.

Limanjaya A Portland-based DJ, producer, and founder of the TOKO TAPE label. As a first-generation Indonesian immigrant who grew up on hip-hop and gospel music, Limanjaya curates sets that bridge gaps between cultures, genres, and time periods, exploring house, hip-hop 12″ records, neo-soul, jazz, and Southeast Asian music.

DJ Snacks Based in Portland, DJ Snacks spins an eclectic, record-heavy mix across decades of rock, indie, and pop, grounded by the timeless grooves of cumbia, jazz, and R&B. She cut her teeth on the pirate airwaves of KPRA and has a regular show on XRAYfm and a long-standing monthly brunch residency at Either/Or.

Prince Klassen Brooklyn-based Prince Klassen learned in the late 90s that music doesn’t have to be linear. With former radio residencies on NY’s The Lot Radio and London’s Soho Radio, and record releases on Japan’s Daily Sessions Records, PK brings house, disco, soul, hip-hop, and turntablism into long-form, deep-listening mixes.

VNPRT Cultivating open-format vibes for 15 years in the Portland scene and abroad, from the Bay to NYC to CDMX. Supporting acts including Ebo Taylor, Sango, and Sasha Marie, VNPRT blends nostalgia with boundary-pushing exploration: boogie, disco, house, global grooves, hip-hop, R&B, and edits.

Andy Warren A club dad and longtime force in Portland’s underground, Andy has spent over a decade building bridges for dancers through his collective Believe You Me and his home base, Process PDX. His sets blur house, techno, disco, funk, and experimental shades into layered, emotional transmissions.

Center for Cassette Studies A collective of two DJs, Karen and Jim, who started spinning together in 2016 at Freeform Portland community radio. They have aired live weekly at KFFP 98.3 FM and worldwide online since then, specializing in intersections of sounds both familiar and unknown: Asian Disco, Nigerian Boogie, Yugoslavian Postpunk, Indonesian Truck Stop.

Daydream Wine and Sound is the official sponsor of the Pickathon DJ program. A bespoke wine bar and high-fidelity listening space rooted in Portland’s music culture, Daydream has been a cornerstone of the city’s community of diggers, dancers, and curious listeners. Their support of the DJ program reflects a shared belief that the best music is the kind that takes you somewhere you didn’t expect to go.
Pickathon takes place July 30 – August 2, 2026 at Pendarvis Farm, Happy Valley, Oregon. Tickets and information at pickathon.com.

stories.t: Pickathon 2026 Neighborhood Reveal: The Paddock & Synthesis
stories.x: America’s Premier Site-Specific Architecture Festival begins the 2026 Neighborhood unveil.
stories.b: Pickathon 2026 Neighborhood Reveal: The Paddock & Synthesis by Scott Edwards Architecture Pickathon is a temporary city of imagination. Every year, we wipe the slate clean. Today, we begin the season-long unveiling of our 2026 Neighborhoods, marking a new chapter for what has become America's Premie
f: Pickathon 2026 Neighborhood Reveal: The Paddock & Synthesis by Scott Edwards Architecture
Pickathon is a temporary city of imagination. Every year, we wipe the slate clean.
Today, we begin the season-long unveiling of our 2026 Neighborhoods, marking a new chapter for what has become America’s Premier Site-Specific Architecture Festival.
Through the Creative Neighborhoods initiative, more than two dozen design teams transform Pendarvis Farm into immersive environments designed specifically for the land they inhabit.

Unlike the usual festival standard of cookie-cutter setups — generic pop-up tents and rental scaffolding — Pickathon’s architecture is designed in direct response to the landscape itself. Every structure is shaped by the contours of the farm, the movement of light through the trees, and the feeling of each space it inhabits.
We don’t just build on the land. We build with it.
The first reveal in this year’s Neighborhood Unveil is the Paddock — Pickathon’s largest open-air gathering space and home to some of the festival’s biggest musical moments.
The Paddock is defined by light and scale.

Throughout the day, the meadow shifts beneath the towering Douglas Firs as sunlight moves across the open landscape. As evening arrives, the space transforms completely — opening into a sprawling gathering place beneath the Oregon sky with distant views of Mt. Hood and the surrounding hills.
For 2026, Scott Edwards Architecture (SEA) returns to reimagine the space with Synthesis, a new stage concept rooted in the movement, rhythm, and modular structure of skateparks.
Following the success of 2025’s “Fractal Forest” installation in the Grove, SEA continues Pickathon’s ongoing focus on placemaking, workforce training, sustainability, and long-term community impact.
Designing For The End Destination First

This project is built through a highly collaborative process where architects, builders, and community partners work as a single team from day one. From the beginning, the design process started with the end destination already in mind: the Q-Side Skatepark in Portland’s Old Town.

Scott Edwards Architecture (SEA) was tasked with creating a permanent modular kit of parts durable enough for the high-impact life of a skatepark while also shaping the immersive visual experience of the Paddock itself.

As the elements of Synthesis come together on the farm, they create a rhythmic, skate-inspired environment that reflects the movement, flow, and spatial experience of a skatepark reimagined as Pickathon’s main stage beneath the Oregon sky.
The architecture is not temporary because it is disposable — it is temporary because it is destined for elsewhere.

After Pickathon 2026, the modular structural elements from the stage will be repurposed into its intended destination — Q-Side Skatepark, extending the life of the project beyond the festival itself and back into Portland’s Old Town neighborhood.
To bridge this street-ready geometry with the landscape of the farm, Garden Fever provides a temporary installation of living plants woven directly into the skate-inspired structure.

This project is powered by a “Partnership Village” with a profound mission. Before a single note is played, the Paddock serves as a high-stakes classroom. Through the Home Building Foundation and their Building to Scale program, youth receive hands-on mentorship, working alongside the pros at Bremik Construction to build the very world you’ll inhabit. Additionally supported by Holmes Engineering, P:EAR, and Garden Fever, we are proving that world-class design is a vehicle for social transformation.

For Pickathon, the Paddock is more than a stage. It’s an example of how music, architecture, mentorship, and community partnerships can come together to create something meaningful both during the festival and long after it ends.
This is the first reveal in the 2026 Neighborhood Unveil, with additional neighborhood concepts arriving throughout the season.
The Lead Visionary: Scott Edwards Architecture (SEA)
Social Impact & Donations: Home Building Foundation

stories.t: Round Two is Here: Pickathon 2026 Expands Its Lineup
stories.x: Quasi, Lyrics Born, Esther Rose, and more join a 26th-anniversary roster that keeps doing what Pickathon does best — honoring the architects while championing what’s next.

f: Quasi, Lyrics Born, Esther Rose, and more join a 26th-anniversary roster that keeps doing what Pickathon does best — honoring the architects while championing what’s next.
We said the first wave was formidable. We meant it. But we weren’t done.

Today we’re announcing the second round of artists joining Pickathon 2026, and if you know how we do things at Pendarvis Farm, you know what that means: more genre-defining legends, more discovery artists pointing toward what music will sound like five years from now, and more reasons to clear your calendar for July 30–August 2.

Quasi, Sam Coomes and Janet Weiss, Portland’s own angular, emotionally raw rock duo, are joining the lineup in a move that feels less like a booking and more like a homecoming. Two decades of catalog, quietly shaping the sound of an entire region.

And then there’s Lyrics Born. The Bay Area hip-hop icon is a performer whose genre-bending showmanship and sheer range have kept him essential across decades. If you’ve never seen him live, this is your moment.
This is where it gets even more exciting, and where Pickathon’s track record speaks loudest. These are artists people will be talking about for years.

Esther Rose continues her rise as one of the most compelling voices in contemporary country and Americana, plainspoken songwriting that lands with real weight. Leroy from the North arrives from Canada with a wry, poetic storytelling style already drawing comparisons to the greats. Meatbodies bring psych-rock wall-of-sound intensity that was practically made for our open-air stages. Sgt. Papers delivers the kind of combustible live energy that ignites rooms. Ora Cogan offers something haunting and precise: gothic atmosphere with real emotional depth. The Takes bring live-wire indie energy, and Nathan Bowles, banjoist, drummer, improviser, rounds out the additions with a one-of-a-kind set that defies easy classification. Fabiano do Nascimento brings his Rio-born, genre-defying guitar work to the farm, weaving Afro-samba and choro with jazz, experimental sound, and ambient electronics into something hypnotic and entirely his own. And Orquestra Pacifico Tropical, Portland’s own psychedelic cumbia force, brings over a decade of electrifying Pacific Northwest stages to Pendarvis Farm for what promises to be a jubilant rhythmic frenzy.

Harrell / The South Hill Experiment / Rumbo Tumba / Friendship / Boy Golden / Hannah Juanita / Sgt. Papers / Channing Wilson / Dylan Earl / Hogslop String Band / El Khat / Esther Rose / Briscoe / Automatic / The Takes / DUG / The Onlies / Ken Pomeroy / Prewn / mercury / Nathan Bowles / Mexican Institute of Sound / PISS / Hannah Hill / Setting / Caitlin Canty / Terror Cactus / Ora Cogan / Jonny’s Day Out / Cosmic Tones Research Trio / Buddy Wynkoop / Portland Songwriters Guild / Orquestra Pacifico Tropical / Rose Gerber / Willam Surly / Honky Tonk Basement / Corndog Cowgirl

There’s a reason people trust the Pickathon process. The War on Drugs, Kamasi Washington, Tyler Childers, The Marías, Black Pumas, Khruangbin, Big Thief… all of them played Pendarvis Farm before they were selling out arenas. That’s not an accident. It’s the result of 26 years of curation built around a single question: who’s pointing toward what’s next?

“We don’t book artists because they’re obvious and everywhere. We book them because they’re pointing to what’s next, and over 26 years we’ve built a community that trusts in the Pickathon process.” — Zale Schoenborn, Pickathon founder

Pickathon is place-making as much as it is programming. Every summer, local design teams transform Pendarvis Farm into a walkable temporary village, including purpose-built stages woven into the forest, intimate fern-lined performance pockets, large-scale wooden structures that blur the line between artist and audience. Nearly every artist performs two distinct sets on different stages. DJs carry momentum between sets. There are literary readings, standup comedy, a full family neighborhood for kids, the intimate 100-seat farm-to-table Curation dining series, and a robust wellness offering including yoga, massage, and dedicated quiet spaces.

Zero-waste operations, reusable serviceware, and site-wide composting have been part of the DNA for years. Free cold water stations, open-air showers, and abundant natural shade keep everyone comfortable. Every ticket gets you the same high standard, the best view at any stage goes to whoever shows up first.
This year’s annual emblem is the frog: joyful, at times a little absurd, and strongest as a chorus of voices. Feels about right. See you on the farm.

stories.t: PICK26: Americana After Dark
stories.x: Country-Gaze, Punk Bluegrass, and Guitar Virtuosos. Explore the wilder side of Americana at Pickathon 2026.
stories.b: As the days get longer, the nights at Pickathon start to take shape. This week's PICK26 is where things stretch out, get loud, and lean a little weirder. From country-gaze to punk-fueled string bands and hypnotic one-man orchestras, this next wave of artists is built for those late-night wanderings
f: As the days get longer, the nights at Pickathon start to take shape. This week’s PICK26 is where things stretch out, get loud, and lean a little weirder. From country-gaze to punk-fueled string bands and hypnotic one-man orchestras, this next wave of artists is built for those late-night wanderings through the woods.
While you’re digging in, two quick updates:
Vendor applications for Pickathon 2026 are officially open.
If you’ve been thinking about joining us on the farm, now’s the time to apply.
Round 2 of the lineup is coming soon.
More artists, more discovery, more reasons to get lost out here.
Start exploring, lock in your plans, and we’ll see you this summer.
Florry is inventing a genre. They take the twang and fiddles of country music but play them with the volume and fuzz of a shoegaze band. It’s loud, joyous, and totally unique.
The future of twang. We booked Florry because they break the rules. They prove that country music can be punk, loud, and weird.

They look like a traditional string band, but they play with the energy of The Ramones. Based in Nashville, they are one of the most entertaining live acts on the circuit, mixing square dance rhythms with wild stage antics.
The riot. We booked them because the festival needs a hoedown. It’s impossible not to have fun at their set.
Hannah Frances is a force of nature. Her guitar playing is intricate and percussive, and her voice is a powerhouse. She writes sprawling, progressive folk songs that demand your full attention.
The “Wow” factor. We booked her because she is technically mind-blowing. Watching her play is a reminder of what one person and a guitar can do.
Using loops, wooden instruments, and native South American sounds, Rumbo Tumba builds massive, danceable soundscapes all by himself. It’s organic techno made with wood and skin.
The hypnotist. We booked him because it’s a magic trick. You won’t believe one person is making all that sound.

The Onlies are a “young” band that has been playing together for 20 years. They grew up in the scene, learning directly from the masters, and now they are the masters. They play traditional Old Time fiddle tunes with the ferocious, sweaty energy of a garage rock band. It’s music that feels ancient but moves with a modern, ripping drive.

We love artists who respect tradition enough to break it. The Onlies don’t treat Old Time music like a museum piece; they treat it like a living, breathing language. We booked them because they possess a rare ability to whip a crowd into a frenzy using nothing but acoustic instruments.

f: Calling all food vendors, makers, and creative businesses—applications for Pickathon 2026 are officially open.

Each summer, the farm becomes a living, breathing village of flavor, craft, and discovery. From unforgettable meals to one-of-a-kind goods, our vendors are a huge part of what makes Pickathon feel like its own world. If you’ve got something special to share, this is your chance to be part of it.

We’re looking for standout food vendors, craft makers, and unique concepts from across the Pacific Northwest and beyond. Whether you’re serving up your signature dishes or creating pieces of lasting beauty, we want to hear from you.
Spread the word. Tell your favorite food truck, your most talented maker friend—or apply yourself.
Join us in the woods this summer!

stories.x: Portland energy, late-night grooves, and the kind of sets you stumble into and never forget… This week’s PICK26 is built exactly for that.

f: Portland energy, late-night grooves, and the kind of sets you stumble into and never forget… This week’s PICK26 is built exactly for that. As we move deeper into Fan Pricing, now’s the time to lock in your passes. Buy Now, Pay Later is available at checkout, making it easier to join us in the woods this summer without missing a beat.
Don’t recognize a name? That is the point. We designed these playlists to be your roadmap. Press play and find your new favorite band before you see them in the woods.
Spotify | Apple Music | Amazon Music | YouTube Music | Tidal

Family Company is a collective of absolute heavy-hitters. They play deep-pocket funk, soul, and R&B with a tightness that only comes from years of playing together. It’s music for dancing, pure and simple.
Every festival needs a backbone. We booked Family Company because they bring the professional-grade groove. You can’t stand still at their set.
Named after a character in The Music Man, this Portland band plays twitchy, nervous, highly danceable art-punk. Think Devo or Talking Heads, but with more caffeine.
We champion the local originals. Buddy Wynkoop captures that specific Portland energy—smart, a little odd, and incredibly fun.

Jonny’s Day Out plays breezy, infectious indie rock that feels like the first day of summer. It’s catchy hooks, bright guitars, and good vibes only. The Portland five-piece creates a live experience that never stays still for too long.
The palate cleanser. We booked them because sometimes you just want to smile. It’s the sonic equivalent of a cold drink on a hot afternoon.
Deep grooves, spacey synthesizers, and improvisation that aims for the stratosphere. This is music for the late-night travelers.
For the deep listeners. We booked them to soundtrack the moments between the moments. It’s the perfect vibe for deep in the night.

f: Experimental jazz, lo-fi poetry, and risk-takers. Meet the artists challenging the status quo at Pickathon 2026.
Don’t recognize a name? That is the point. We designed these playlists to be your roadmap. Press play and find your new favorite band before you see them in the woods.
Spotify | Apple Music | Amazon Music | YouTube Music | Tidal

Mary Halvorson is widely considered one of the most innovative guitarists of her generation. She plays jazz, but deconstructs it—bending notes, shifting rhythms, and creating sounds you didn’t think a guitar could make.
We book for the brain, too. Pickathon audiences love to be challenged, and Mary provides the intellectual fireworks. Watching her play is like watching a master painter at work.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO

Hudson Freeman makes music that feels like it was recorded on a cassette tape in a living room. It’s fragile, beautiful, and deeply personal. In a loud world, his music is a whisper you have to lean in to hear.
The “Anti-Festival” act. We booked Hudson because his music creates an immediate intimacy. It turns a crowd of hundreds into a private conversation.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO
This LA duo (Baird and Goldwash) is impossible to pin down. They mix funk, indie rock, electronic, and jazz into a blender. It’s playful, virtuosic, and totally unpredictable.
We love the risk-takers. We booked them because they play with a sense of freedom that is infectious. They are the band you see when you want to be surprised.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO
The project of Izzy Hagerup, Prewn makes slow-burning, explosive indie rock that recalls the raw emotion of the 90s. It’s wobbly, distorted, and incredibly cathartic.
For the emotional release. We booked Prewn because the songs feel massive. It’s the perfect soundtrack for looking up at the stars and feeling everything at once.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO

This is the supergroup of the underground, comprising Nathan Bowles (banjo/keys), Jaime Fennelly (harmonium/synths), and Joe Westerlund (percussion). Setting isn’t just ambient; it is a collision of trance, jazz, and deep improvisation. They build “organic drone” structures that lock into hypnotic rhythms, creating a sound that feels like a mix between a spiritual jazz record and a UFO sinking into a peat bog.

Pickathon has always been a haven for the “heads”—the people who want to close their eyes and go somewhere else. Setting is the ultimate immersive band. We picked them because they force you to slow down and listen. In a weekend of high stimulation, their set will be a necessary, psychedelic “sound bath” that resets your nervous system.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO

Spotify | Apple Music | Amazon Music | YouTube Music | Tidal

A Nevada City native and Portland icon, Alela Diane writes folk songs that feel ancient and timeless. Her voice is clear as a bell, cutting through the forest air with stories of motherhood, nature, and memory.
Pickathon royalty. Alela’s music sounds like it grew out of the ground at Pendarvis Farm. We booked her because she creates a sacred silence in the crowd that is rare and beautiful.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST  |  ARTIST BIO

A Cherokee songwriter from Oklahoma, Ken Pomeroy brings a unique perspective to the folk tradition. Her music is sparse, haunting, and incredibly mature for her age, blending modern indie influences with her heritage.
The truth-teller. We love Ken because she doesn’t hide behind production. It’s just her and the song. She represents the next wave of diverse voices reclaiming American folk music.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST  |  ARTIST BIO

Caitlin Canty writes songs that sound like travel. Her music is restless, gritty, and beautiful, driven by a voice that has a touch of smoke in it. She bridges the gap between old-time string bands and modern songwriters.
We booked her for the craft. Caitlin is a musician’s musician—impeccable guitar playing and songwriting that never wastes a word.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST  |  ARTIST BIO

From the legendary heartbeat of reggae to the next great voice of the blues, plus alt-country storytellers and groove-heavy Southern soul
f: Some music doesn’t chase trends, it carries stories. This week’s PICK26 spotlight is all about artists who keep those roots alive while pushing the sound forward. From the legendary heartbeat of reggae to the next great voice of the blues, plus alt-country storytellers and groove-heavy Southern soul, these are artists who understand where the music comes from and where it can go next.
Meet the musicians bringing deep heritage and fresh fire to the farm this summer.
HAVE YOU SECURED YOUR EARLY-BIRD TICKETS, YET?

The early believers always know. Early Bird pricing is the lowest you’ll see all year, and the forest is filling up fast. We don’t expect it to last much longer. These early prices are your chance to lock in your summer plans at the best price!
If you’re planning to be here, now’s the time.

As a member of The Gladiators in 1970s Jamaica, Clinton Fearon helped build the foundation of roots reggae. His bass lines are legendary, and his voice carries the warmth and wisdom of a life spent in the groove.
We honor the architects. Having Clinton on the farm is a blessing. We booked him because his music radiates a positivity that is contagious. You walk away from his set feeling lighter.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO

At only 25, D.K. Harrell channels the spirit of B.B. King with eerie precision. He plays the big-band, soulful blues that feels almost extinct in the modern world. He isn’t revitalizing the genre; he’s embodying it.
We booked him to prove a point: The Blues isn’t a museum piece. D.K. plays with a fire and authority that demands attention. He is going to be a superstar, and you’ll want to say you saw him here.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO
Led by Dan Wriggins, Friendship writes songs that feel like short stories—specific, observant, and deeply human. They mix Americana instrumentation with the pacing of slowcore indie rock.
They are a “musician’s band.” We love them because they don’t rush. In a world of short attention spans, Friendship forces you to lean in and listen to every word.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO
Ben Chapman sits right at the intersection of 70s jam-band rock and country soul. It’s loose, greasy, and full of swagger. Think Little Feat or The Allman Brothers, but for 2026.
We need the groove. We booked Ben because his band is a well-oiled machine. It’s perfect afternoon music—cold drink in hand, sun on your face, head nodding to the beat.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO

DUG is the meeting point between American Old Time and Irish Folk. The duo features Lorkin O’Reilly (from Dublin) and Jonny Pickett (from California), blending the storytelling wit of Irish ballads with the rugged, foot-stomping rhythm of American roots music. It’s unapologetically modern folk that makes you want to hug your friends and order another round.

We are always looking for that perfect afternoon energy—music that is warm, funny, and incredibly skilled without taking itself too seriously. We booked them because their chemistry is infectious; you feel like you’re sitting in on a private jam session between two best friends who happen to be virtuosos.
🎧 LISTEN ON THE PICKATHON 2026 PLAYLIST | ARTIST BIO

stories.t: PICK26: For The Night Owls
stories.x: Prepare for the heavy side of Pickathon. Doom metal legends Acid King, the Mexico City party of MIS, and psychedelic discovery.
stories.b: Some weeks, we go light and breezy. This is not that week. PICK26 is for the night owls, the heavy heads, and anyone who's ever stood in front of a wall of amplifiers and felt completely at peace. We're talking doom metal legends, a Mexico City dance party, junkyard psychedelia built from scrap meta
f: Some weeks, we go light and breezy. This is not that week. PICK26 is for the night owls, the heavy heads, and anyone who’s ever stood in front of a wall of amplifiers and felt completely at peace. We’re talking doom metal legends, a Mexico City dance party, junkyard psychedelia built from scrap metal, and desert noir cumbia that sounds like a mirage you can dance to. These are the artists we book when we want Pickathon to feel less like a festival and more like a ritual.
Early bird tickets are on sale now! Grab yours while they last and save on the lowest priced tickets of the year.
The Vibe: The Riff That Never Ends

Legends of the stoner/doom metal scene, Acid King plays music that feels like a slow-moving landslide. It’s heavy, psychedelic, and mesmerizingly loud. Frontwoman Lori S. crafts guitar tones that you don’t just hear; you feel them in your chest.

Pickathon has a secret love affair with heavy music. We booked Acid King because the festival needs to be shaken to its foundation. This is the set for the people who want to close their eyes and get lost in the sheer physical power of sound.
The Vibe: The Mexico City Dance Floor

Camilo Lara mixes vintage Mexican cumbia and mariachi samples with modern electronica and hip-hop beats. It’s a chaotic, joyful, high-energy collage of Mexico City’s past and future. Think LCD Soundsystem, but with accordions and political bite.
We need a party starter. We booked M.I.S. because they turn concerts into raves. It’s smart, subversive music that tricks you into dancing until you’re sweating.

From Tel Aviv by way of Yemen, El Khat builds their own instruments out of trash and scrap metal to play traditional Yemeni folk melodies with a punk ethos. It sounds clanky, raw, and totally hypnotic.
This is the “Discovery” pick of the week. We love them because they sound like nothing else on earth. It’s a reminder that music can be made out of anything, as long as it has soul.

Born in Buenos Aires and based in Seattle, Terror/Cactus plays psychedelic cumbia that sounds like the soundtrack to a mystic western movie. It’s dubby, atmospheric, and full of reverb-drenched guitars.
We booked them for the vibe. They are the perfect late-night band—music that feels like a mirage shimmering in the heat.

stories.t: Beyond the Breaking Point: How a Dead End Led to the “Third Way”
stories.x: Discover how Creative Neighborhoods is revolutionizing festival design through circular architecture—turning temporary stages into permanent community landmarks.
stories.b: The Dead End For twenty-five years, Pickathon has used the woods as a laboratory. We've always been obsessed with the idea of a festival that leaves a legacy instead of a footprint. But following the 2023 festival, we hit a wall. We were faced with a choice that wasn't really a choice at all. The ri
f: For twenty-five years, Pickathon has used the woods as a laboratory. We’ve always been obsessed with the idea of a festival that leaves a legacy instead of a footprint. But following the 2023 festival, we hit a wall.

We were faced with a choice that wasn’t really a choice at all. The rising tide of global costs meant that the traditional way of building our immersive neighborhoods had reached a dead end. We looked at the “Generic Path”—rented stages and corporate tents—and knew it would make money, but it wouldn’t be Pickathon. We also knew that simply raising ticket prices to an elite level would price out the very community that gives the festival its life.

In 2024, we launched Creative Neighborhoods. We realized that the only way forward was to decouple the Moment (the four-day festival) from the Movement (our year-round mission). The “Third Way” stops treating architecture as a temporary expense. Instead, we treat it as a permanent investment. By separating these costs, we keep the festival accessible while supercharging our ability to build world-class environments.
The “Third Way” is already happening. In 2025, we took the first major steps toward this vision:
The Windmill Neighborhood: Vendor booths were reverse-designed to be reassembled as greenhouses for the Oasis Day Shelter.
The Grove: Modular structures were built as a “Kit of Parts” that now serve as permanent community infrastructure and seating.
The Circular Engine: How it Works
Our process is built on a cycle of Reverse-Design. We are moving from our history of upcycling toward a future where every Neighborhood has a permanent home secured before we even begin.
The Permanent Vision: We work with Founding Partners to design a masterpiece—a garden sanctuary, a workspace, or a public landmark—engineered for a 10+ year lifespan.
The Kit of Parts: We decode that design into a modular system of high-quality building blocks.
The Festival Foundry: Over a dozen professional teams build the functional elements—the stages, spas, and bars integrated into the farm’s landscape.
Life-Changing Mentorship: Aspiring designers, makers, and artists work alongside elite professionals through the entire design, build, and reassembly cycle.
The Final Delivery: The components are reassembled at their final destination as permanent community assets.
While every neighborhood will continue to use this model, we are now seeking a select group of visionaries to anchor our inaugural 2026 scale-up.
Founding Partners: We are looking for private, nonprofit, and civic partners with a project budget for permanent structures—from garden sanctuaries to public shelters.
Professional Build Teams: We are making a final call for architects and master builders to lead our 2026 neighborhoods and mentor the next generation of creatives.

stories.t: PICK26: The Future of Music
stories.x: From hip-hop with purpose to psychedelic cumbia, glitchy pop, and raw punk energy, this week’s Vanguard picks are for the curious, the adventurous, and anyone ready to discover what’s next.
stories.b: The future is loud, colorful, fearless, and already on its way to the farm. This week's PICK26 lineup is all about artists rewriting the rules, bending genres, and pushing music somewhere new. From hip-hop with purpose to psychedelic cumbia, glitchy pop, and raw punk energy, this week's Vanguard pic
f: The future is loud, colorful, fearless, and already on its way to the farm. This week’s PICK26 lineup is all about artists rewriting the rules, bending genres, and pushing music somewhere new. From hip-hop with purpose to psychedelic cumbia, glitchy pop, and raw punk energy, this week’s Vanguard picks are for the curious, the adventurous, and anyone ready to discover what’s next. Plug in, press play, and meet the sounds of tomorrow.
Early bird tickets are on sale now! Grab yours while they last and save on the lowest priced tickets of the year.
The Vibe: Cumbia from Another Dimension

Eblis Álvarez is a mad scientist. Based in Bogotá, the Meridian Brothers take the traditional rhythms of Colombian Cumbia and run them through a filter of surrealism, theatrical electronics, and avant-garde humor. It’s familiar rhythmically, but sonically, it feels like it’s being beamed in from a futuristic carnival.

Pickathon has always championed the weirdos. We love Meridian Brothers because they prove that “traditional” music doesn’t have to be preserved in amber; it can be torn apart and rebuilt into something wild. This is going to be the set where you look at your friend and mouth, “What is happening?” while unable to stop moving your feet.
The Vibe: The New Sound of Rio

If Marcos Valle is the history of Brazil, Ana Frango Elétrico is the future. A rising star in the Rio scene, Ana blends chamber-pop, boogie, and indie rock into a sound that is colorful, queer, and impossibly vibrant. It’s music that feels like a confetti cannon going off—lush production, catchy hooks, and a charismatic energy that has made them a critical darling worldwide.

We booked Ana to bring the color. Their sound is pure dopamine—a joyful, art-school energy that refuses to take itself too seriously. It fits perfectly in this “Vanguard” week because it redefines what Brazilian pop music can look like in 2026.

In a world of mumble rap and vibes, Sa-Roc is a technician. She is an emcee in the classic sense—every syllable is placed with surgical precision, and every verse has a purpose. Backed by booming, golden-era production, she delivers conscious hip-hop that hits you in the chest. It’s powerful, spiritual, and incredibly commanding.

Pickathon has a long history of booking hip-hop artists who can control a live band environment (Digable Planets, GZA). Sa-Roc fits that lineage perfectly. We booked her because we want you to feel empowered. Her set isn’t just a performance; it’s a transfer of energy.

This is what the internet sounds like. mercury blends glitchy hyper-pop, alternative R&B, and grunge into a sound that refuses to sit still. It’s chaotic, emotional, and completely of the moment. If you want to know what the next generation is listening to, this is it.

To challenge you. We don’t just book “easy” music. We booked mercury because they are pushing the boundaries of what a “song” structure can be. This set is for the sonic adventurers who want to see the blueprint of pop music being rewritten in real-time.

Sometimes you just need to scream. PISS brings the raw, distorted, aggressive energy of the underground punk scene. It’s loud, it’s fast, and it’s not interested in being polite. This is the set where the mosh pit opens up and the room gets sweaty.

Catharsis. A festival is a release valve, and we need bands that let you let it all out. We booked PISS to be the shot of espresso in the middle of the weekend. It’s a reminder that Pickathon still has sharp teeth.

stories.x: A Valentine’s special featuring Thee Sinseers, The Womack Sisters, and Widowspeak. Discover the romantic side of the 2026 lineup.
